chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) dispatched to his wives twelve Owqiya and one Nash, and the Owqiya is forty Dirhams, and the Nash is half the Owqiya, being twenty Dirhams. So that was five hundred Dirhams.' I said, 'By our weighing?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

key_terms.أُوقِيَّة: Owqiya, a unit of weight/money equivalent to forty Dirhams
key_terms.بِوَزْنِنَا: By our weighing, referring to the local standard weight measurement
key_terms.دِرْهَم: Dirham, a silver coin and unit of currency
key_terms.نَشّ: Nash, a unit of weight equal to half an Owqiya (twenty Dirhams)

ai.seo_question: What was the specific weight and value of the dowry given by the Prophet to his wives?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the Prophet Muhammad’s (SAWW) practice of providing a standardized dowry of 520 dirhams to each of his wives, serving as a foundational legal precedent for *mahr* in Shia jurisprudence. By confirming the equivalence of the Owqiya and Nash weights with local standards, it underscores the importance of adhering to traditional metrological norms in financial transactions. This specific valuation highlights the Prophet’s emphasis on fairness and consistency in marital contracts, influencing later scholarly discussions on the minimum and recommended amounts for dowries.
